page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-3xL40S is an x86_64 architecture server powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical AMD EPYC 9575F cores running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via three NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a total of 144 GB of VRAM. This server does not include local storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics. Memory bandwidth is strong, ranking in the top 25% for both cached small-block and uncached large-block read and write operations. The system also excels in data processing, achieving top-tier results in bzip3 decompression, Geekbench image and text processing, and Passmark database operations. For artificial intelligence workloads, the hardware achieves top-tier LLM inference speeds, processing 6061.83 tokens per second for prompt processing and 129.38 tokens per second for text generation using a medium 7B model.

A primary hardware tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage solutions for persistent data. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dense integration of three enterprise-grade GPUs alongside a high-capacity memory array offers a specialized resource profile for parallel computing without the overhead of dedicated CPU pinning. This configuration is suited for large-scale LLM inference, parallelized data processing, ray tracing, and database operations.
